summary:
AstroHealth is a web-based Astronaut Health Monitoring System designed to support astronaut health awareness during space missions. The project provides a centralized dashboard to monitor important health indicators, including heart rate, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, and sleep duration.

The system includes a Mission Control Intelligence Panel that displays health information, identifies unusual readings, generates alerts, and provides an illustrative rule-based health risk assessment. It also includes a NASA Research & Data section that connects the project's features with important astronaut health research topics such as cardiovascular changes, sleep disruption, oxygen monitoring, and space radiation.

AstroHealth aims to demonstrate how digital health monitoring and data visualization can help organize astronaut health information and support awareness during long-duration space missions. The current prototype uses simulated health readings and is designed as an initial demonstration that can be expanded with real sensor data and validated research datasets in the future.
details:
1. Project Overview

AstroHealth is a web-based Astronaut Health Monitoring System designed to demonstrate how astronauts' physiological information can be organized and monitored during space missions. The project aims to support astronaut health awareness and help mission operators identify unusual changes in simulated health readings.

2. How the System Works

AstroHealth provides an interactive dashboard displaying four important health indicators:

  • Heart Rate (BPM)
  • Blood Oxygen Saturation (SpO₂)
  • Body Temperature (°C)
  • Sleep Duration (hours)

The system includes a Mission Control Intelligence Panel that displays health readings, generates alerts when configurable demonstration thresholds are exceeded, and calculates an illustrative rule-based health risk score. Users can test different health scenarios, view changes in readings, and export monitoring data as a CSV file.

3. NASA Research Integration

The project includes a NASA Research & Data section covering cardiovascular health, sleep disruption, oxygen monitoring, and space radiation. It provides links to NASA research resources, including the NASA Open Science Data Repository, NASA Human Research Program, and NASA Technical Reports Server.

4. Technology Used

AstroHealth was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Notepad was used for code editing, Google Chrome for running and testing the application, and ChatGPT for AI-assisted planning, coding guidance, troubleshooting, and documentation.

No physical medical sensors or hardware are currently connected. The prototype uses simulated health readings.

5. Innovation and Expected Impact

The creative aspect of AstroHealth is its combination of health visualization, simulated monitoring scenarios, automated rule-based alerts, risk assessment, and a dedicated Mission Control interface in one application.

The project demonstrates how an accessible digital platform could help organize astronaut health information and support awareness during long-duration space missions. Future development could include wearable sensor integration, validated health-analysis algorithms, and compatible spaceflight research datasets.

AstroHealth is an educational prototype, not a clinically validated medical device or an operational NASA monitoring system.
